text.p: **BIRTHDAYS**
German psychiatrist Baron RICHARD VON KRAFFT-EBING was born in 1840. He published pioneering studies of sexual aberrations in "Psychopathia sexualis".
American inventor and subway engineer BION ARNOLD was born in 1861.
British novelist JOHN GALSWORTHY, who wrote "The Forsyte Saga", was born in 1864.
South Australian motor manufacturer Sir EDWARD HOLDEN was born in 1885. His family company amalgamated with General Motors to produce Holden cars.
Australian cricket star JACK GREGORY was born in 1895. He once scored a century in 70 minutes against South Africa, and was also a successful fast bowler.

One of Australia's pioneering radio and television producers HECTOR CRAWFORD was born in 1913. In showbusiness circles he was known as "The Silver Fox". He began his career as an orchestra leader and introduced the "Music for the people" concerts and became the conductor of the Australian Symphony Orchestra.
British guitarist with the Byrds DAVE CROSBY was born in 1941. He was also a founding members of the band Crosby, Stills and Nash.
British singer SARAH BRIGHTMAN was born in 1961. She is the ex-wife of ANDREW LLOYD WEBBER and is best known for her role in his musical "Phantom Of The Opera".
**EVENTS**
1040 : King DUNCAN of Scotland was murdered by MACBETH,
who then became king and ruled for 17 years.
1457 : The first book ever printed was published. It was
"The Book of Psalms" produced by a wandering astrologer named FAUST.
1863 : The first kanakas arrived in Brisbane from the

Pacific Islands. They were transported by Captain ROBERT TOWNS who wanted to start a cotton industry in Queensland. This form of indentured labour was abolished in 1904 and within three years, most of the kanakas had returned to their islands.
1893 : France became the first country to introduce motor
vehicle registration plates.
1900 : The Boxer Rebellion ended when Allied forces

stormed Peking. The Allied force was made up of 10,000 men from international forces and rescued the Europeans who had been under seige for 56 days. The Chinese Emperor and Empress DOWAGER fled the city.
1905 : The legality of the Australian flag was questioned
in Britain. The King had not given his approval.
1907 : Uproar followed a decision by Australia's federal
politicians to vote themselves a 50 percent pay increase from 400 pounds a year to 600 pounds.
1908 : World's first international beauty contest was
held at the Pier Hippodrome at Folkestone, England.
1920 : King ALBERT of Belgium opened the seventh Olympic
Games in Antwerp.
1930 : The Church of England gave a cautious go-ahead for

the use of birth control. The decision followed weeks of debate by the bishops. The Encyclical Letter from the Archbishop of Canterbury called for strict controls over the sale and advertising of contraceptives.
1932 : One of Hollywood's best known canine stars, RIN
TIN TIN, died.
1936 : A school athletics team in Sydney had its badge
banned. The Hurstville Central School had worn the ancient Sanskrit symbol of the swastika as its emblem.
1945 : Japan accepted the Allies' terms of unconditional
surrender, ending World War Two.
1945 : The secret of radar was disclosed in London.
1947 : Pakistan became independent from India, satisfying
demands for a separate Muslim state.
1948 : DON BRADMAN's final test cricket game started in
London.
1951 : An Auckland man who killed his young bride was
jailed for life. GEORGE HORRY married EILEEN TURNER after convincing her he was an English secret agent. She sold her home and they married. He killed her the next day and cashed the cheque.
1956 : The British Air Force had a close encounter with a

UFO. The unidentified flying object was picked up on radar and seen by the naked eye at Lakenheath. An RAF pilot reported seeing the object streak beneath his aircraft. Radar picked up the stationary object, which suddenly accelerated northwards at

965 km per hour. The pilot made airborne contact with the object, only to have it move behind his fighter. Failing to shake the craft the pilot called in a second aircraft, at which point the UFO moved off and all radar contact was lost.
1960 : JACK BRABHAM won the Formula One drivers'
championship for the second consecutive year. The greengrocer's son from Sydney was nicknamed "Black" JACK.
1969 : The first British troops entered Northern Ireland.
1980 : Polish workers took over the Gdansk shipyard in
Poland.
1983 : Australia's ROBERT DE CASTELLA won the Olympic
marathon at Helsinki.
1986 : The daughter of executed politician, ZULFIKAR ALI
BHUTTO, was jailed. BENAZIR BHUTTO was imprisoned by Pakistani dictator General ZIA.
1989 : Australia defeated England 4-0 in the ASHES test

cricket series. Australian bowler TERRY ALDERMAN secured several lbw decisions during the tour, leading a British graffiti artist to make an addition to a "THATCHER OUT" slogan written on a subway wall. It finally read : "THATCHER OUT - lbw Alderman".
1994 : International terrorist "Carlos the Jackal" was
arrested in Sudan and handed over to French authorities, to stand trial over the bombing of a French drug store in 1979.
1996 : The National Party, the architects of South
African apartheid, moved to the opposition benches for the first time in 48 years.
